transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because I’m having a really hard time keeping things organized. It’s not like I’m trying to be messy, but between my schoolwork and this little accessories shop I’m trying to run, everything kind of ends up in piles—supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes—and then I just don’t know what I’m supposed to do first.  

I feel a little embarrassed saying that, because it probably sounds simple, but it’s been getting hard to manage.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind and make it hard to focus?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like thoughts that feel intrusive or scary or anything. My mind does jump around a lot, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. It’s more just… a lot happening in my head, I guess. Does that answer it okay?
Did you have trouble staying organized when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so, at least from what I’ve been told. My mom actually still has some of my elementary school notes from teachers, and they say things like I was always getting out of my seat, talking before I was called on, and kind of rushing through group activities.

I don’t think I was trying to be difficult or anything—I usually understood the work—but I guess I had trouble, um, doing it in the organized way everyone expected. Does that count?
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks after you’ve started them?

Yeah… I mean, not every single time, but it does happen more than I’d like. Like if a teacher gives me a few steps for an assignment, or someone in a vendor meeting tells me what needs to be done, I’ll usually do the first part okay.

But then later I’ll realize I missed something important, like I forgot to attach a form, or I didn’t finish the last part of an order note. It’s embarrassing because I thought I had done it, or at least started it well. I don’t know if that counts as not finishing, but… yeah, I guess I do have trouble following it all the way through sometimes.
Do these organization problems cause trouble in more than one part of your life, like both school and your business?

Yeah… I think it does, unfortunately. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s affected school stuff and also my shop projects.

Like, I missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid might be at risk, which is… really stressful. And with the shop work, people have started kind of relying on me less because I’ll miss parts of what needs to happen. I feel bad about it, because I’m not trying to be careless. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are you often easily distracted by things going on around you?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I notice things around me, like anyone does, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m often distracted by them.

Maybe it depends on the situation? I don’t want to overstate it. What kind of distractions do you mean?
Even in a quiet setting, do you often find your attention drifting away from what you’re trying to do?

Yeah… I think so. Even if it’s quiet, like in class or if I’m watching a video for business assignments, I can start out really trying to pay attention.

But then a few minutes later I’ll notice I’m thinking about charm designs or order ideas instead, and I’m like… wait, I missed half of what they just said. It’s not like I’m trying to ignore it. It just kind of drifts. Is that what you mean?
Did these attention and organization problems get a lot worse only after a specific stressful event?

I don’t think it was like one specific stressful event, no. It’s more like… it started becoming a real problem after I changed schools, maybe a little over two years ago.

I had to manage the business program and my accessories shop with less structure, and that’s when it got harder to keep everything together. So… about two years and a couple months, I guess. Does that answer it okay?
Do you often feel anxious or worried even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like all the time or for no reason.

I mean, I get worried if there’s actually something going on, like something I need to handle, but I wouldn’t say I’m just anxious when there isn’t a problem. At least I haven’t really noticed that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
